title: 面向2035的高中教育规模波动与扩容应对

abstract: 面向2035年，高中教育呈现规模骤增骤减、结构多元融合、区位向城镇集聚的发展态势。高中学龄人口即将迎来峰值，教育扩容已迫在眉睫。但扩容并不仅依靠新建学校来增加学位供给，还需统筹应对多重复杂矛盾：规模扩大和质量提升的双压叠加、人口向城区流动与县中振兴向镇区集中的双向交织、人口客观波动和家长选择偏好的双重影响，以及学龄人口骤增骤减带来的双重挑战。研究认为，高中教育扩容可从三个层面推进：一是可持续性扩容，统筹短期紧缺与长期冗余做好系统研判；二是差异性扩容，找准全局中的区域方位；三是韧性扩容，通过增强扩容的韧性来保障学位刚性需求。

title: Ethical Judgments About Difficult History: How Jewish-Israeli Students Engage Ethically With the Israeli–Palestinian Conflict
abstract:
This study analyzes Jewish-Israeli students’ historical ethical judgments (HEJ) about the 1948 War—a formative and difficult history within the Israeli–Palestinian conflict—and how those judgments shifted following the outbreak of the Israel–Gaza War in 2023. Using a mixed-methods approach, it draws on two rounds of data collection: just before the Israel–Gaza War (
N
 = 373) and months later (
N
 = 214). Findings show major differences in students’ HEJ and the changes between students who graduated from secular or religious education systems. After the war began, all subgroups—despite pronounced secular-religious differences—exhibited a notable decline in their judgment quality. The study suggests that historical thinking is more context-dependent than previously assumed and introduces an analytical framework for HEJ in diverse international contexts.

title: Interpreting Null Effects in Education: Insights from a Tutoring Experiment
abstract:
We learn not only from when interventions work—but also from why they do not. Policymakers embraced high-impact tutoring to address pandemic learning loss, but scaling promising practices is difficult, and not all implementations prove effective. Using random assignment, we find null (math and a low-stakes reading test) and negative (−0.09
SD
on state reading scores) impacts from assignment to a virtual tutoring program. Using frameworks for interpreting null results in education experiments, we identify subject-specific heterogeneity and contribute to the literature on dosage challenges for in-school tutoring. We also identify alignment of tutoring content with classroom instruction as a moderator warranting further study. This paper offers strategies for uncovering mechanisms behind unexpected results and designing theory-driven, policy-relevant evaluations.

title: Impact of Workforce-Oriented Performance-based Funding on Students’ Return on Investment
abstract: States are increasingly using workforce-oriented performance-based funding (PBF) to fund higher education and incentivize colleges and universities to improve students’ postgraduation outcomes. In this study we use detailed up-to-date data on workforce-oriented PBF policies in the United States combined with publicly available College Scorecard data to estimate the effect of PBF on students’ return on investment, as measured by debt-to-earnings ratios and loan default rates. We find that workforce-oriented PBF has minimal effects on students’ debt-to-earnings ratios and loan defaults except at historically Black colleges and universities, where we find suggestive evidence that workforce-oriented PBF reduced student debt.

title: Bureaucracy and Burden: Understanding Take-up of a Need-Based Financial Aid Program
abstract: Social programs, including college financial aid, often reach only a fraction of eligible beneficiaries. We examine this problem through the lens of Michigan’s Tuition Incentive Program (TIP), a state need-based grant aid program. We conduct a large-scale mixed-methods study using data on more than 1 million Michigan public school students and 55 interviews with program administrators, high school counselors, and financial aid staff. We find that while one third of Michigan high school graduates are eligible for TIP, only ~30% of TIP-eligible community college students receive the aid, limiting its impact on affordability. We identify key barriers that shape take-up: the presence of administrative burdens and fractured and ill-defined administrative responsibility, which constrains the ability of front-line administrators to alleviate these burdens.

title: “Don’t Go West”: An Afropessimist Examination of Black Students’ Experiences Off Campus
abstract: Black collegians’ experiences of racism at historically white institutions are well documented in higher education research. However, few studies have investigated their racial realities in off-campus spaces near historically white institutions. Drawing on a qualitative intrinsic case study, this work examines Black undergraduates’ experiences in and navigation of a college town with a history of anti-Black terrorism. More specifically, I use the anti-Black spatial imaginary, an Afropessimist perspective, to elaborate the structure of Black suffering beyond university boundaries. Findings illustrate that anti-Blackness—the paradigmatic position of Blackness as subhuman—renders Black students’ socially dead in off-campus spaces through the following themes: (a) Blackness as trespasser, (b) Blackness as object of surveillance, and (c) Blackness as target of violence.

title: Fractured Identities: Narratives Showing Raced-Classed Psychological and Social Costs of Economic Mobility for Students in Meritocratic Systems
abstract: Using narrative analysis of two students, this longitudinal study examines raced-classed experiences of mobility as students transition to college, revealing the costs of macro-meritocratic educational systems on micro levels. Findings showcase that after developing early academic identities, students experienced fracturing of academic identities from social identities in high school followed by raced-classed misperceptions of their identities in college. Mobility pathways in meritocracies contributed to “a split” not only among their identities but also in “the difference” between their families and future, which carried both promise and loss. Findings suggest the need not only to address raced-classed structures in educational pathways but also to adopt new national discourses and measurements of mobility that attune to costs and academic environments of mobility.

title: Leading Inclusive Schools for Students with Disabilities: A Systematic Review of Principal Leadership in the United States
abstract: A growing body of research provides evidence that principals play an important role in creating and sustaining inclusive schools for students with disabilities. We synthesized 19 studies within the United States from 1995 to 2024, examining the practices principals use to create and sustain inclusive schools. Most studies provided insights into the challenges principals confront and specific leadership practices they used to advance inclusion for students with disabilities under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act. Many studies were qualitative and focused on elementary schools in urban contexts. We present areas of practice principals used to create and sustain inclusive schools and offer a critique of this body of research with implications for future research, policy, and practice.

title: Untangling Faculty Turnover: Exploring Retention and Attrition at Historically Black Colleges and Universities
abstract: Historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs) have made significant contributions to American higher education. Despite the essential role of faculty in higher education and talent development, HBCUs face an increasing threat of faculty attrition. Inspired by the social exchange theory, which focuses on the exchange and reciprocal dynamics between parties, this study leverages empirical survey data to explore the reasons faculty choose to remain at, return to, or depart from HBCUs. Findings indicate that faculty attrition at HBCUs is driven by the pursuit of better career opportunities, enhanced research support, and a more favorable institutional environment. Conversely, faculty retention is influenced by altruistic motivations and advantaged development opportunities. The study provides several implications for improving faculty retention at HBCUs.

title: Exploring Perceptions of Organizational Change Processes in Becoming a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI)
abstract: Demographic shifts in the college-going population led to the establishment of Hispanic-serving Institutions (HSIs)—colleges and universities eligible for competitive federal funding based on 25% enrollment of Hispanic students. But beyond enrollment and grants, HSIs must evolve to intentionally serve Latine students. Using emergent strategy, a justice-based framework about how social actors change organizations, and in-depth interviews with 28 participants, we examined their perceptions of change processes associated with intentional efforts to serve Latine students. Findings reveal five processes: (a) implementing HSI grants, (b) responding to student needs, (c) collaborating for change, (d) being resilient through setbacks, and (e) envisioning new HSI futures. This study offers practical implications for change agents seeking to intentional transform their institutions.

title: Critical Data Use for Just Democratic Governance: The Case of School Boards
abstract: While data-driven decision making holds promise for fostering more equitable and just education, existing research also highlights its potential to perpetuate deficit perspectives, reinforce prevailing educational ideologies, and misattribute the roots of disparities—thereby deepening inequities. This study explores these tensions through a qualitative study of 10 school board members, a group frequently overlooked in educational research. Grounded in democratic and critical theoretical frameworks, this paper examines how board members engage with data and the degree to which their practices challenge or sustain systemic inequalities, concluding with considerations for democratic governance.

abstract:

Mixed-effects meta-regressions investigated the role of measurement, publication, sample features, and outcome (i.e., academic achievement, creativity, attitudes and emotions, school and classroom climate, and moral development). Overall, Waldorf students performed significantly better (

Waldorf students had significantly greater academic achievement and reported a significantly better school and classroom climate, with differences in aesthetic creativity, attitudes and emotions, and moral development not being statistically significant. title: What are Special Education Teachers’ Roles?
abstract: The purpose of this review was to systematically examine research on the roles of special education teachers (SETs), including how they or others conceptualize their roles and how they enact those roles in K–12 contexts. Drawing on cultural historical activity theory, we analyzed 80 qualitative, quantitative, and mixed-methods studies published from 1997 to 2025. We found that SETs fulfill a wide array of instructional, collaborative, and case-management roles and enact these roles in widely varied ways. This variability emerges from both individual and organizational factors because SETs enact their roles in educational systems marked by competing priorities, constrained resources, and ambiguous aims. Together these problems create structural barriers to SETs’ agency and, consequently, their ability to fulfill their responsibilities in a way that provides students with disabilities with access to equitable, inclusive learning opportunities.

title: A Systematic Review of Universal Screening Measures for Social, Emotional, and Behavioral Strengths and Concerns
abstract: Universal screening for social, emotional, and behavioral strengths and concerns is a critical component of a multitiered systems of support framework. To ensure psychometrically defensible and equitable screening practices, schools must adopt screening measures with strong evidence for their intended use. In this review, we systematically describe available universal social, emotional, and behavioral screening measures’ features psychometric evidence, and evidence for use with culturally and linguistically diverse students, specifically within the framework of the Consensus-Based Standards for the Selection of Health Measurement Instruments. Our search process resulted in the identification of 79 measures across 186 studies within 170 records. We describe the features of these measures and synthesize psychometric evidence, concluding that measures with a wide range of features and evidence are available; however, evidence is largely limited to select measurement properties. This underscores the importance of the evidence-based selection of measures and expanded inquiry into the technical adequacy of measures with diverse populations.

title: How Dominant Conceptualizations of Leadership and Identity Have Shaped the Research on Women in Educational Administration Over Time: A Descriptive Review
abstract: Women, particularly women of color, are underrepresented in virtually all educational administration positions in the United States. Simultaneously, dominant discourses persist upholding masculinity and Whiteness in educational administration and highly ranked and influential journals, thus limiting who has access to, and can thrive in, leadership. With nearly 40 years since the last review on women and other minoritized identities in educational administration, this descriptive review traced the research on women in educational administration in the United States in dominant journals from 1 year before the review by Yeakey et al. review until 2023 and yielded 89 studies. Key findings from the reviewed corpus include (a) small, slightly growing scholarship on women in educational administration, (b) disrupted use of critical frameworks and limited challenges to dominant discourses in administration, (c) few studies including other marginalized and/or minoritized identities or extending past the gender binary with the exception of increased scholarship on African American/Black women leadership, and (d) the persistence of discriminatory systems, creating barriers for women, especially women of color, in leadership.

title: Questioning the Credibility of Educational Meta-Analyses: Insights From Multimethod Reanalyses
abstract:
This study investigates the credibility of meta-analyses published in the
Review of Educational Research
from 2012 to 2022 by surveying effect-size inflation, statistical power, heterogeneity, and analytic reproducibility using classical and robust Bayesian methods. A corpus of 362 separate meta-analytic effects derived from 76 published articles was included. Data from a subset of 53 articles with 189 effects were reanalyzed; 94% of experimental effects and 79% of observational reported correlations exceeded the magnitude of those reproduced using robust Bayesian estimates. The difference in the magnitude of the mean reported effect sizes and correlations was substantially larger than those reproduced using robust Bayesian methods (ranging from 29% to 267%). Median retrospective power was extremely low in experimental research, with only 4.21% of meta-analyses exceeding Cohen’s .80 threshold using robust Bayesian estimates; observed power based on 10,672 primary-study effects indicated that only 29.0% met this benchmark. Observational studies demonstrated comparatively higher power, with 53.3% surpassing Cohen’s .80 threshold using robust Bayesian estimates, and 68% of the 8,189 correlations sufficiently powered to detect their reported correlation strength. Median heterogeneity remained high across designs, with
I
2
values exceeding 80% in experimental and 90% in observational meta-analyses. Just over half (55.3%) of meta-analyses initially shared sufficient data, increasing to ~70% following email request. Only ~5% shared sufficient code for partial analytic reproduction. These findings identify potential concerns regarding effect-size inflation, statistical power, heterogeneity, and data and code availability that may constrain reproducibility in educational meta-analyses.

title: Mapping Ladson-Billings’s Tripartite Framework in a Systematic Review of Culturally Relevant Pedagogy for Black Students
abstract: Developed through inquiry into successful teaching with Black students, culturally relevant pedagogy (CRP) requires student learning, cultural competence, and sociopolitical/critical consciousness, yet the published literature represents these commitments unevenly. We systematically reviewed 30 empirical studies of CRP-related practice in U.S. K–12 classrooms involving Black American students, published from 1995 through May 2022. We mapped study-level representation of Ladson-Billings’s three components, synthesized student outcome evidence, and descriptively summarized first-author and published-record characteristics. Academic achievement/student learning appeared in 24 studies, cultural competence in 22, sociopolitical/critical consciousness in 6, and all three components in 5. Thirteen studies reported qualifying student outcome evidence; seven provided at least one Black-specific outcome or an all-Black focal sample, and none independently operationalized sociopolitical analysis or critical agency as a distinct student outcome. Claims about CRP depend on correspondence among component representation, documented pedagogy, student evidence, population attribution, and design-permitted inference.

title: Teacher Roles and Work Contexts in Higher Education: A Scoping Review
abstract: An empirical overview of teacher roles in higher education that shows the versatility of the teaching profession, specifically considers context, and may stimulate collaboration is lacking. This study acts on current research and practice gaps by conducting a review to provide a new professional image of the higher education teaching profession, addressing the following research questions (RQs): (RQ1) Which roles and work contexts of teachers are found? (RQ2) What is empirically known about the content of these teacher roles found within various work contexts? and (RQ3) Which combinations of teacher roles and contexts occur, and how do they relate to each other? A scoping review was conducted including 139 peer-reviewed records. Fifteen primary roles of higher education teachers were identified, mainly targeting students. Roles differed per context based on content, name, existence, or perspectives. Different role combinations were identified, but only three articles mentioned the possibility of dividing these roles between two teachers.

title: Physical Activity Interventions Embedded Within University Teaching and Learning: A Scoping Review
abstract: Embedding physical activity into the university curriculum offers a way to address students’ typically high sedentary behaviour. While some interventions have been trialled, the heterogeneity of methods precludes synthesis of results. This review aimed to document the methods used for assessing embedded physical activity or sedentary behaviour interventions to summarise existing research and identify methodological gaps. Four databases were searched for peer-reviewed articles. Of the 7345 citations screened, 28 studies were included, describing two intervention types: active breaks (n = 15), involving short movement breaks, and physically active learning (n = 13), involving active workstations (e.g., sit-stand desks). Small-sample feasibility studies were common and quality-assessment ratings often were low. Outcome measures included physical activity, academic performance, and feasibility. Few studies collected qualitative data or investigated teaching staffs’ experiences. To better inform design, implementation, and evaluation of future evidence-based interventions, carefully controlled studies engaging a range of university stakeholders are needed.

title: From Metrics to Meaning: Advancing QuantCrit as an Anti-Racist Intersectional Praxis in Educational Research
abstract: This guidance paper advances quantitative critical race theory (QuantCrit) and intersectionality as inseparable frameworks for liberatory critical inquiry and praxis in systematic reviews and meta-analyses in educational research. Drawing on the intellectual genealogies of Black social scientists, Black feminist theorists, and critical race scholars, we interrogate the ontological, epistemological, axiological, and methodological commitments that structure traditional quantitative approaches. We synthesize recent systematic reviews and meta-analyses that engage QuantCrit, identifying promising practices, recurring tensions, and areas of conceptual conflation. As a guidance paper, we center the methodological decisions that organize evidence synthesis, including search strategies, inclusion criteria, coding, aggregation, interpretation, and reporting. We demonstrate how QuantCrit and intersectionality can be enacted across these stages through multidimensional critical reflection on positionality and accountability, citational and epistemological justice, AI ethics and transparency, historical and spatial contextualization, redistribution of power in knowledge production, and liberatory praxis. We conclude with strategies for embedding QuantCrit and intersectionality as inseparable critical inquiry and praxis (QCII-CIP) in systematic reviews and meta-analyses, urging scholars to move beyond conventional, unexamined metrics and checklists toward evidence synthesis that resists the reproduction of racial and intersectional inequity and supports more just futures in educational research.

title: The (In)Visibility of Social Interactions in the Digital Classroom: A Review of Research on Digitally Mediated K–12 Science Instruction in the United States from 2012 to 2022
abstract: K–12 science instruction increasingly occurs in classrooms where students grapple with scientific content through individual computers. This shift toward the widespread use of digital devices occurred simultaneously with science education reforms that have pushed for students’ engagement in science practices. In this review, I explore how empirical research has studied interactions in digitally mediated science classrooms at the nexus of reform in both science education and classroom technology. I find that many studies investigated individuals’ interactions with content or devices, absent studying social interactions between students and teachers. Additionally, many studies did not clearly illustrate students’ engagement in the science and engineering practices enumerated in the Next Generation Science Standards. I conclude by highlighting studies that defied these trends by richly investigating the social sphere of digitally mediated instruction. Ultimately, I call for more research in this mold to interrogate instruction mediated by commercial educational technologies that have come to saturate modern science classrooms.

title: Adaptive Support for Collaborative Learning: A Meta-Analysis
abstract:
Collaborative learning is widely recognized in educational research as an effective pedagogical approach for facilitating the development of a broad range of skills. However, this approach also faces several challenges in ensuring optimal learning outcomes. Adaptive instructional support has emerged as a promising solution for addressing these problems by enhancing both individual- and group-level learning. This meta-analysis of 83 empirical studies builds on an integrated theoretical framework to examine the effects of adaptive instructional support on different learning dimensions as well as the moderating role of design features, learner characteristics, and contextual conditions in collaborative learning. Overall, adaptive instructional support exhibited a positive medium effect (
g
 = .73, 95% CI [.56, .90],
p
 < .001) on collaborative learning with varying effects across learning dimensions. Design features proved the most influential moderator: Adaptations based on cognitive variables, implemented through cognitive models or data-science approaches, targeted at collaborative activities, and applied over short-term durations yielded the strongest effects; however, the role of teacher and learner involvement in decision-making around adaptivity requires more careful consideration. Learners’ prior knowledge, domains, and learning context also significantly moderated the effectiveness of adaptive support.

title: Education in Written Popularization Skills for Higher Education Students: A Literature Review
abstract: In this literature review, we detail the effectiveness of teaching interventions for popularization writing on the (self-reported) popularization writing skills of university students. We included studies that focused on written popularization skills, that empirically tested the effect of the educational materials on (the self-perception of) writing skills, that detailed the educational materials that were being tested, and that focused on undergraduate or graduate university students as participants. Interventions for popularization writing mostly have a positive effect on the measured and self-reported writing skills of university students. This is irrespective of the pedagogical framework and educational materials that were used.

title: Toward Equitable Community College Student Pathways in STEM and CTE: An Integrative Literature Review
abstract: Community colleges are pivotal in expanding access to both science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) and career and technical education (CTE). These pathways are closely interconnected in practice because many programs blend scientific, technical, and applied learning, and students frequently move across these transfer- and workforce-oriented pathways simultaneously. Yet, research and policy historically have examined STEM and CTE as separate domains, limiting understanding of how students experience these interconnected educational ecosystems. Bringing these literatures into closer dialogue can reveal broader structural and developmental processes shaping community college pathways and student success. Accordingly, this integrative review examines empirical and theoretical scholarship across STEM and CTE to provide a comprehensive picture of community college pathways and their implications for equitable education. We conclude with recommendations for institutions and educators to strengthen supports and suggest future directions for research, policy, and practice.

title: Expanding Access, Negotiating Boundaries: Opportunity Hoarding in Catholic Schools under Voucher Expansion
abstract: The Indiana voucher program has the potential to increase access to private schooling by removing the barrier of the cost of tuition. In doing so, vouchers have many implications for enrollment patterns in Catholic schools, potentially disrupting otherwise homogenous school communities. Such changes could prompt boundary-making as parents seek to secure educational opportunities for their children amid change. Yet Catholic schools’ commitment to religious mission and the common good may temper exclusionary responses to change. Drawing on interview data from 59 private Catholic school parents, this study explores how parents’ perceptions of school change shape symbolic boundary-making and opportunity hoarding. Findings indicate that parents’ attitudes toward the voucher program, perceptions around academic quality, and the religiosity of their schools evolved as voucher policy expanded. In response to these perceptions, parents constructed social boundaries between voucher and non-voucher students, public and private schools, and families perceived as academically or religiously aligned with their school community. These boundaries were at times uncertain or contested. Parents frequently expressed ambivalence, navigating tensions between their religious beliefs, the Catholic mission of their schools, and their desire to secure educational advantages for their children. This study contributes to the literature on symbolic boundary-making and opportunity hoarding by demonstrating that these patterns can be partial, uncertain, or contested.

title: Educational Systems and Inequality in Attainment across 27 Low- and Middle-Income Countries, 1990 to 2017
abstract:
To what extent do macro-institutional characteristics influence the equalization of educational outcomes by social origin? Motivated by this long-debated question, I investigate the relationship between the
destandardization
, or decreasing standardization, of educational systems and socioeconomic inequality in secondary educational attainment across 27 low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). Here, destandardization captures the degree to which educational policies and responsibilities are not uniform across subnational authorities or schools within a country. I combine unique country-level measures of destandardization with cumulative cross-sectional household survey data comprising 931,749 observations across 414 country-cohorts, observed near the age of secondary-education completion, covering 1990 to 2017. Contrary to proponents’ expectations, the findings suggest that in highly destandardized subnational systems, the attainment gap between the richest and poorest individuals is substantially wider than in systems with minimal destandardization. This association is weaker at the school than at the subnational level. These results remain consistent across multiple specifications, including alternative definitions of age groups and cohort exposure. I argue that macro-institutional changes alone may be insufficient to overcome the foundational challenges facing LMIC education systems, such as poverty and underinvestment, and to address socioeconomic disparities in educational outcomes.

title: Living with permanent temporariness: School principals' sensemaking and sensegiving under ontological uncertainty in a refugee‐receiving context
abstract:
Abstract
This study examines how school principals make sense of and communicate demographic change under ontological uncertainty, where it remains unclear whether change is temporary or a durable reconfiguration. Using an exploratory single‐case design, we analysed interviews with 27 principals and 20 teachers across six Turkish provinces receiving students under temporary protection. Findings reveal a four‐dimensional architecture of sensemaking leadership comprising sensemaking, sensegiving, perceived organizational consequences, and difficulties and facilitating strategies. Principals relied on enactment, selection, retention, and counterfactual scenario building, while sensemaking extended across school boundaries through informal networks. Participants retrospectively described crisis becoming routine as demographic change became embedded in everyday school life, though weak institutional support repeatedly returned interpretive responsibility to individual leaders. The study introduces ontological uncertainty as a distinct condition of educational leadership and shows how prospective sensemaking operates when the status of change remains unresolved.

title: Private school choice as moral legitimation: Risk, responsibility and parenting in Türkiye
abstract:
Abstract
This study investigates how parents in Türkiye justify their decision to enrol their children in private schools and negotiate this choice in relation to their awareness of educational inequality. While critical school choice scholarship, particularly research conducted in England, has examined the moral and affective tensions between being a good parent and a good citizen, this article considers how these tensions are negotiated in a different policy context. Drawing on qualitative interviews with 17 private school parents, analysed through reflexive thematic analysis and informed by a governmentality perspective on risk and responsibilisation, alongside affective–discursive practice, I examine how private schooling becomes a morally defensible choice in a context where state policies have supported private provision and educational competition is shaped by high‐stakes examinations. Participants described perceived academic, social and institutional risks associated with public schooling, while presenting private schools as offering security, responsiveness and socially compatible environments. In these accounts, private schooling could appear as a parental obligation rather than simply a preference. Although 15 participants acknowledged that private schooling deepens educational inequality, they differed in how they reconciled this recognition with their choices. Some legitimised their decisions through appeals to necessity, parental care or responsibility beyond the individual family, while five expressed sustained moral conflict. The findings suggest that moral legitimation can reconfigure, without necessarily eliminating, the moral tensions of school choice, as decisions experienced as necessary may simultaneously reproduce privilege and social boundaries.

title: Pistols and pride flags: How gender matters for boys in Welsh relationships and sexuality education
abstract:
Abstract
School‐based relationships and sexuality education (RSE) is a site of intense discursive circulation around the concept of gender. In the 2020s, international RSE curricula are responding to increasing visibility and cognisance of gendered and sexual diversity among young people and attempting to address gender‐based inequities and violence. Simultaneously, expansive RSE curricula are also the targets of sustained assault from ‘anti‐gender’ movements, which assemble diverse phantomatic fears—including crises of masculinity, reduced religious influence, the corruption of notional childhood innocence and reduced parental influence over access to sexuality education—into furious attacks on LGBTQ+ rights, feminism and RSE itself. These moves are typically framed as protecting young people but paradoxically ignore their lived experiences and persistent calls for more comprehensive education around gender and sexuality. Grounded in this hopeful yet fulminous international context, this paper asks what else can be learned about gender's discursive circulations from young people's negotiations of school‐based RSE. The paper offers a rhizoanalytic orientation to gender, entangling imaginaries of gender discourses in RSE as a waveform, and gender fears as phantoms with data produced during a doctoral project exploring teachers' negotiations of a new statutory, rights‐based national RSE curriculum in Cymru/Wales. Within rhizoanalysis, assemblage theory is deployed to explore how gender became salient during one event within a participatory, arts‐based RSE ‘creative audit’ at a Welsh secondary school. An encounter between two Year Ten (aged 14–15) boys, a toy pistol, a Pride flag and a teacher is engaged multiply through written analysis and a series of assemblage maps to explore the ways in which gender—differentially constituted across theorised assemblages—emerges, informs and shapes situated talk and interactions. The paper considers the challenge and promise of engaging boys in rights‐based education, and the role of teachers in fostering inclusion, tackling homophobia and addressing gender‐based violence, within a shifting cultural milieu where these inequities are gaining traction across diverse political and educational contexts.

title: Beyond compliance: Professional curiosity and the cultivation of research‐informed practice
abstract:
Abstract
This paper examines the relationship between embedded practitioner enquiry and teacher professional agency in a special education school in the northeast of England. Drawing on a research practice partnership with the school, we develop the concept of ‘professional curiosity’, which we define as a sustained professional investigative orientation connecting externally produced research evidence and the localised demands of specific classroom contexts, and as a lens through which to understand how school cultures can foster genuinely research‐informed practice. Data were generated through semi‐structured interviews with eight members of teaching staff and analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. We address two interrelated questions: how a culture of embedded classroom‐based research might shape professional curiosity, and how professional curiosity as a concept might then underpin research‐informed practice in a school environment. Findings suggest that professional curiosity develops through a processual shift from compliance to intrinsic inquiry, sustained by collaborative structures and ecological conditions that protect it from the pressures of performativity. Conceptually, we show how professional curiosity connects core beliefs about what it is to be a teacher, to professional expectations at an institutional level, and how this inquiring stance can become an important expression of teacher identity. The study contributes an original theorised construct to debates around teacher agency, practitioner enquiry and research‐informed practice, with implications for school leadership and professional development in contexts where accountability and compliance can take precedence over teachers' investigative orientation.

title:

AI
in higher education: A multi‐level analytical framework
abstract:
Abstract

This conceptual paper extends existing theorization of
affective chronopolitics
to examine how AI technologies become implicated in the governance of educational subjects, institutions and imagined futures in higher education. In particular, we argue that AI‐mediated temporalities may involve different manifestations such as immediacy, anticipation, acceleration or delay, while their affective dimensions may encompass anxiety and fatigue as well as relief and hope. Building on scholarship on chronopolitics, affect and educational governance, we develop a multi‐level analytical framework spanning the micro level of lived experience and subject formation, the meso level of institutional organization and responsibility and the macro level of policy imaginaries and governance. The framework foregrounds how AI technological capacities become translated into affective‐temporal norms and how their benefits and burdens are unevenly distributed in higher education. We suggest that this framework offers a heuristic for empirical research into how AI reorganizes affective and temporal arrangements in higher education.

title: Beyond satisfaction: Perceived contribution to learning as a mediator between supervisory relationships and students' self‐reported research competence
abstract:
Abstract

The expansion of master's education, alongside digital‐native learners and AI‐supported academic training, has created new demands for supervisor–student relationships. Existing evidence on how such relationships shape student development remains inconclusive. This study moves beyond linear models to examine how two relational dimensions, supervisory affiliation (i.e. emotional closeness) and supervisory influence (i.e. supervisor direction/control), shape the self‐reported research competence of 522 Chinese master's students. Our findings reveal a supervisory paradox: While supervisory affiliation is consistently associated with research competence regardless of disciplinary and institutional contexts, supervisory influence demonstrates an inverted
U
‐shaped relationship with research competence. Notably, these relations are exclusively mediated by perceived contribution to learning, whereas student satisfaction shows no significant mediating function. This implies that effective supervision might be characterized by its internalized learning value instead of its affective appeal. These findings challenge the widespread use of student satisfaction to evaluate supervisory quality. We propose that departments adopt relational diagnostic tools to align expectations and ensure that guidance is not only provided, but effectively received and internalized by students.

title:
Partial correspondence between mathematics achievement and multidimensional well‐being‐related profiles: Evidence from
PISA
2018 in Türkiye
abstract:
Abstract
Academic achievement is a central educational outcome, but students' well‐being, motivational resources and relational experiences provide distinct information about their educational lives. This study examined whether multidimensional well‐being‐related profiles correspond with mathematics achievement among 15‐year‐old students in Türkiye. PISA 2018 data from 6749 students in 186 schools were analysed using weighted, complex‐survey‐adjusted latent profile analysis of 14 prespecified indicators spanning core well‐being outcomes, academic‐motivational resources and risks and relational experiences. A four‐profile solution was retained and then refined by allowing limited local dependence among conceptually close indicators. Two large intermediate profiles differed mainly in parental emotional support; a smaller profile showed broadly low functioning and relational disadvantage; and another combined high well‐being and resources with high competition. Mathematics achievement was highest in the High Parental Support–Near Average in Other Domains profile (469.92) and lowest in the Broadly Low Functioning and Relational Disadvantage profile (421.74). The profile with the broadest favourable well‐being and resource pattern had the second‐highest mathematics mean; its 12.20‐point difference from the highest‐achieving profile was small (approximately 0.14 SD), and top‐quartile probabilities produced the same ordering. The findings indicate partial rather than complete correspondence: achievement broadly aligned with favourable well‐being‐related patterns but did not map one‐to‐one onto the multidimensional profiles. This person‐centred evidence suggests that academic achievement and students' broader well‐being‐related experiences provide related but non‐equivalent information about educational success.

title: Better academic performance in high school, more class skipping in higher education?

Class skipping occurs more frequently in general courses than in specialized courses. Individual self‐efficacy and student leadership activities could help explain the above findings. These findings highlight the significant role of high school academic performance in HE class skipping, with important implications for improving the match between curriculums and student needs.

title:
A network psychometric analysis of teachers'
AI
adoption profiles and occupational perceptions
abstract:
Abstract
Teachers' responses to artificial intelligence (AI) are mostly studied through intention‐based acceptance models, where a binary contrast between users and non‐users leaves the differences inside each group out of view. Occupational variables, when considered, are typically examined one at a time. This study applied diffusion of innovations theory to move beyond the user/non‐user dichotomy towards empirically derived adoption profiles, and modelled occupational perceptions as an interconnected network instead of as separate variables. Data from the TALIS 2024 AI module were analysed for 54,276 teachers across 55 education systems. Latent class analysis of teachers' AI use, attitudes, and barriers identified five distinct profiles corresponding to the theory's adopter categories. A mixed graphical model estimated the unique association between profile membership and each of 12 occupational perceptions. Perceived societal value of the profession emerged as the strongest correlate (edge weight = 0.24), three to five times larger than any other; self‐efficacy played a secondary role. Perceived value tracked openness to AI rather than actual use, while indecision and principled rejection concentrated among those feeling undervalued. Value was highest among teachers who had internalised AI pedagogically, not merely used it instrumentally. Beyond self‐efficacy and well‐being, these findings position the perceived standing of the teaching profession as a central condition for AI adoption. Policies that address how the profession is valued may therefore be as consequential for integration as those targeting skills or infrastructure.

title: Profiling teachers' digital technology use: The role of professional and organisational factors and associations with instructional quality
abstract:
Abstract
Drawing on professional capital and pedagogical affordance perspectives, this study examines teachers' digital technology use and its associations with professional and organisational factors and instructional quality. Data were drawn from 4251 secondary school teachers in Hong Kong and Macao who completed the PISA 2022 teacher questionnaire. Latent profile analysis identified three ordered profiles characterised by low, moderate and high levels of digital technology use. The largely parallel response patterns across the nine indicators indicate that heterogeneity was predominantly level‐based rather than configurational. Multinomial logistic regression showed that digital professional development, instructional leadership and professional collaboration were associated with profile membership, with professional collaboration showing the strongest and most consistent association. Associations with digital professional development also varied across forms of participation. A one‐way MANOVA further showed significant differences across profiles in adaptation of instruction, teacher feedback and assessment of student learning, with higher‐use profiles reporting higher levels on all three dimensions. These findings show that meaningful heterogeneity in teachers' digital technology use may take the form of ordered differences in overall levels of digital technology use rather than qualitatively distinct patterns of practice. They also highlight the importance of professional and organisational conditions in differentiating teachers' levels of digital technology use and suggest that greater use may provide more opportunities to realise pedagogically relevant affordances in teaching. The study therefore advances understanding of teachers' digital technology use by linking level‐based heterogeneity to the professional contexts in which it is situated and to key dimensions of instructional quality.

title: Exploring cradle to career initiatives' plausibility as a strategy to tackle place‐based inequities
abstract:
Abstract
Internationally, cradle to career (C2C) initiatives are gaining traction as a way of tackling spatial concentrations of poor education and related outcomes. Targeting high‐poverty neighbourhoods, they aim to bring together local schools, services and community groups; create seamless, locally bespoke supports for children from birth to early adulthood; and simultaneously improve outcomes across multiple interrelated domains—education, health and well‐being and material security. Yet, there has been little consideration of how far C2C initiatives present a plausible (i.e. strategically convincing) approach to tackling neighbourhood‐level inequities. Very little is known about how even the most well‐established C2C initiatives intend to bring about change. Addressing this gap, this paper develops a qualitative interpretative analysis of C2C initiatives' plausibility. Focusing on the English ‘Pipeline Places’ (pseudonym) C2C initiative, it scrutinises the Theories of Change developed by schools and services leading Pipeline Places in four neighbourhood sites. The theories outline each site's starting situation, desired outcomes and proposed mechanisms of change. Further, they surface three main tensions that threaten Pipeline Places' plausibility: positioning individual behaviour change as a ‘solution’ to structural problems; focusing on deficits without acknowledging assets; and an imbalance between targeted and universal support. The paper argues these are not just local design limitations but reflective of wider conceptual challenges facing the field. In response, it identifies conceptual tools, drawn from thinking on relational power and systems change, which C2C initiatives can use to explore how to address these tensions. This advances the field's capacity to develop contextually grounded and strategically plausible initiatives.

title: How behaviour and motivation mediate the impact of school absences on achievement
abstract:
Abstract

Using longitudinal data from England, linking the National Pupil Database (NPD) school register data with Millennium Cohort Study (MCS) survey data (

In particular, externalising behaviour, risky behaviour and educational motivation each mediate part of the association between school absence and achievement, whereas prosocial behaviour and self‐esteem do not. These findings were replicated using comparable data and analytic methods in Wales, providing further support for the robustness of the findings. The results suggest that responses to school absence should continue to prioritise supporting pupils to recover missed learning, while recognising that behavioural and motivational support may also help to mitigate the impact of absences on achievement.

title: Parental Migration During Childhood and Later‐Life Major Depressive Disorder
abstract:
Abstract
The rise of migration in many communities across the Global South raises questions about its consequences for the children of migrants. Previous studies have primarily examined the immediate impact of parental migration on children's well‐being, while its cumulative effects across the life course remain largely unknown. Drawing on retrospective life histories, prospective monthly residency data, and novel diagnostic measures of mental disorders from the longitudinal Chitwan Valley Family Study in Nepal, this study examines the relationship between parental migration during childhood and later‐life onset of major depressive disorder (MDD). Results indicate that parental migration during childhood is associated with a reduced risk of developing MDD across the life course, although this benefit is exclusive to the younger cohort. These findings suggest that in a context where migration is prolific, parental migration may serve as a protective force against adverse mental health outcomes in later adolescence and adulthood, thus revealing a potential source of long‐term inequality in high out‐migration countries such as Nepal.

Abstract
Return migration remains understudied in the migration–fertility literature, despite returnees accounting for up to 25 percent of all international movements. This article examines whether the fertility patterns of return migrants—a highly mobile population experiencing at least two moves: migration and return—resemble or diverge from those of nonmigrants in their countries of origin. Using a unique cross‐country dataset encompassing four diverse socioeconomic and migration contexts (Argentina, Romania, Senegal, and Ukraine), we examine three key fertility outcomes: timing of first birth, completed fertility, and childlessness. Our findings reveal a general pattern of similarity between returnees and nonmigrants across nearly all contexts. A singular exception is that the transition to the first child is significantly delayed during the migration period. However, our evidence demonstrates that this disruption is largely a temporal effect, as a robust recuperation effect is observed upon return. Furthermore, although large and statistically significant delays occur during migration among women in Ukraine and men in Argentina and Senegal, these do not necessarily translate into a permanent reduction in family size. Specifically, return migrants in most groups register completed fertility similar to those of nonmigrants.

title: Assessing the Quality of the Family Interrelationship Variable in Classificatory Kinship Populations
abstract:
Abstract
The family interrelationship variable is widely used to study household structure, child fostering, and intergenerational support. Yet its measurement validity has not been assessed in populations with classificatory kinship systems—prevalent across most of sub‐Saharan Africa—where kinship terminology groups relatives by generation rather than by direct biological link.
This study provides the first empirical assessment of this variable in a West African classificatory context. Using genealogical data from the SLAM  (Suivi Longitudinal au Mali ‐ Longitudinal survey in Mali) survey in rural Mali, linked at the individual level to the 2009 national census, we compare census‐reported relationships to the household head with genealogically reconstructed ties among the Bwa, who follow a classificatory terminology. The results reveal systematic and directional discrepancies: nephews, nieces, and stepchildren are frequently reported as biological children of the household head. These findings highlight how the imposition of Western nuclear‐family categories in classificatory kinship settings produces nonrandom biases, leading to inflated counts of household head's children and underestimation of extended family ties.

title: Commonalities and Differences in Lowest‐Low Fertility Patterns
abstract:
Abstract
Lowest‐low fertility has been extensively studied, particularly in the Global North. Much less is known about whether these patterns will repeat across other regions of the world. As demographic theories evolve to explain recent trends, there is a growing need to understand how emerging patterns of fertility decline in the Global South might be (dis)similar to past trends observed in the Global North. Using an empirical approach, we examine 34 countries that experienced a period total fertility rate (TFRp) ≤ 1.3 for at least one year between 1950 and 2023, with the aim of identifying common patterns and possible trajectories. The findings reveal heterogeneous yet comparable dynamics: after initially spreading at the end of the 20th century, the diffusion of lowest‐low fertility appeared to stall. However, since the early 2010s, the number of countries with TFRp ≤ 1.3 has increased, affecting both more and less developed countries. Our cohort analysis suggests that additional countries may soon join this group. We argue that lowest‐low fertility results from the combination of declining early fertility and the absence of compensatory increases in late fertility. These processes should be examined starting from different theoretical explanations, with attention to differences between more and less developed countries.

title: The Demographic Impact of Leadership: Mayoral Education and COVID‐19 Excess Mortality in Italy
abstract:
Abstract
During the COVID‐19 pandemic, excess mortality rose sharply across Europe, with striking territorial disparities even within countries. This paper examines whether the characteristics of locally elected officials influenced excess mortality in Italy—one of the first countries severely affected. Using weekly death statistics and a Bayesian hierarchical spatiotemporal model, we estimate excess mortality at the municipal level. To address endogeneity in political selection, we exploit close mayoral elections within a regression discontinuity design. Results show that college‐educated mayors significantly reduced excess mortality during the first wave by lowering both the likelihood and the rate of excess deaths, but not during the second wave. Analysis of newly collected large‐scale datasets on municipal policy activity and social media communication points to two possible channels: timely and more targeted local policy responses, and less alarmist, more guidance‐oriented public communication. Interpreting mayoral education as a proxy for broader leadership traits, such as rapid and non‐alarmist responses to crisis, the findings highlight how political selection can shape local demographic vulnerability and population resilience during acute mortality shocks.

title: Capturing Demographic Burden Over Time with the Cumulative Dependency Ratio
abstract:
Abstract
The age dependency ratio is widely used to summarize population structure and to inform discussions of economic potential and population aging. However, as a period measure, it reflects the demographic balance at a single point in time and is highly sensitive to the timing of fertility and mortality change. This paper introduces the cumulative dependency ratio, a longitudinal reinterpretation of the traditional indicator that aggregates person‐years lived in dependent and support ages over a specified horizon. By explicitly incorporating the temporal dimension, the cumulative dependency ratio provides a person‐year‐based summary of demographic burden and facilitates comparison across periods, regions, and demographic scenarios. Using examples for the United States alongside comparative analyses across world regions, the paper illustrates how a cumulative perspective smooths short‐term demographic fluctuations, reduces sensitivity to the choice of observation year, and reframes the relationship between population structure and long‐run economic performance. Viewed through this cumulative framework, future fertility changes primarily affect the timing of dependency rather than its cumulative magnitude, and long‐run differences in demographic burden across regions appear smaller than implied by period measures. The cumulative dependency ratio complements existing indicators by providing an interpretable summary of sustained demographic pressures and intergenerational balance.

title: Reducing Health Inequality by Increasing Children's Education: A Two‐Generation Mediation Approach and Evidence from the United States
abstract:
Abstract
Recent research indicates that adult children's education may influence their parents’ health at older ages. However, a critical population‐level inequality question remains understudied: Would improving children's education increase or reduce parental health inequalities? To answer this cross‐generational inequality question, we analyze longitudinal data from the United States Health and Retirement Study using multilevel marginal structural models and well‐defined causal estimands. We find that educational inequalities in five parental health conditions would be reduced if their children obtained more education. In particular, the health disadvantages for the least educated (i.e., with less than 12 years of schooling) parents would decrease by 14–37 percent. Meanwhile, the health advantages for college‐educated parents do not seem to change. This reduction in health inequality is evident independent of how children's education is measured (e.g., the highest, lowest, average level, or based on a randomly picked child). We discuss two sociodemographic mechanisms—namely, the effect heterogeneity and distribution mechanism—through which the inequality reduction effects manifest. Our research joins a growing recognition of increasing education across generations as a strategy to improve population health and reduce health inequalities in the United States and elsewhere.

title: Joint Land Titling and the Marital Bond in Southwestern Uganda
abstract:
Abstract
When a randomized intervention in southwestern Uganda offered fully subsidized land titles to agricultural households, the majority of husbands chose to add their wives’ names to the title, a striking result given the persistent gender asymmetry in land ownership across Africa. This study investigates the social dynamics underlying that result, asking: What does a joint land title mean for couples in practice, and do women benefit as intended? We draw on fieldwork observations, conversational interviews with selected couples, and interviews with community leaders. Our findings indicate that women's marital bargaining power increases, consistent with household bargaining models. Critically, we identify an additional channel: a joint title symbolizes a husband's commitment to his spouse and marriage. This symbolic dimension is crucial, as women's property rights are threatened under marital insecurity. Joint titling thus shapes marital dynamics not only by strengthening women's bargaining power but also by encouraging what we term “cooperative power”—a fortified marital bond that inspires investment in the marriage. By applying ethnographic approaches to numerical outcomes, the study shows how qualitative inquiry complements survey research in examining the meanings, motivations, and social logics underlying observed demographic and economic behaviors, offering insight into family processes in contemporary Africa.

title: Rethinking Fertility Responses to Armed Conflict: A Critical Review of Conflict–Fertility Research in Low‐ And Middle‐Income Countries
abstract:
Abstract
Current research on armed conflict and fertility has produced varied results, with some studies finding short‐term fertility declines and others observing subsequent rebounds. Drawing on 27 empirical studies from low‐ and middle‐income countries, this review assesses how conflict exposure is conceptualized and measured, evaluates the theoretical frameworks applied across the literature, and identifies pathways linking conflict to fertility outcomes. We find that established fertility theories were developed under assumptions of institutional stability that armed conflict systematically disrupts, and that no single theoretical framework is sufficient to explain the full range of conflict–fertility relationships documented in the literature. To clarify these pathways, we propose a multilevel conceptual framework connecting conflict to fertility outcomes, showing that seemingly contradictory findings arise because armed conflict operates through multiple simultaneous pathways at macro‐, meso‐, and micro‐levels that can suppress or accelerate fertility depending on conflict type, duration, and intensity. Lastly, the review identifies the risk of conflict exposure misclassification, particularly when recurrent low‐intensity violence is treated as a discrete shock, or when exposure measures ignore duration and proximity. Advancing research will require stronger theoretical grounding, more precise theory‐based measurement, and greater attention to whose reproductive intentions are being realized and under what conditions.

abstract: 美丽城市是从降碳、减污、扩绿、增长4个维度所形成的城市生态环境高水平保护、自然资源高效率利用、经济社会高质量发展、人与自然和谐共处的城市可持续发展新范式，是一种既富又美的可持续高韧性城市，是美丽中国建设之鼎。以人地耦合共生论为理论基础，以常美常富为奋斗目标，以城市更新为重要实践手段。国内外美丽城市研究在概念内涵认知、监测评估体系确立和多样化建设路径等方面取得了阶段性进展，但总体尚处在初级研究阶段。美丽城市建设的概念与内涵正在逐步深化、监测评估体系逐步确立、建设路径日趋多样，但还缺乏美丽城市建设的差异化指标体系与标准体系，绿色低碳发展标准引领不足。未来应重点开展美丽城市建设的差异化指标体系与智能跟踪评估的研究，核算美丽城市建设的生态安全阈值并进行智能协同调控，研发美丽城市建设的智能决策支持系统与绿色发展集成模式，协调好美丽城市建设中的“更美”与“更新”关系，以美丽城市为鼎推进美丽中国建设。

title: 国家绿色发展示范区建设历程与监测评估指标体系研究——以北京城市副中心为例
abstract: 北京城市副中心建设国家绿色发展示范区，是首都功能疏解、京津冀协同发展与城市绿色低碳转型多重战略耦合推进的重要实践。随着示范区建设持续推进，副中心绿色发展评价亟需从以建设目标落实和阶段性成效判断为主，转向兼顾动态监测、标准支撑、风险预警和协同治理的综合评估。现有指标体系以“绿色生产—绿色生活—绿色生态”为基本框架，为目标管理和成效评价提供了重要依据，但对气候适应、城市运行安全、跨区域生态环境共治及绿色制度创新等内容刻画不足，难以充分支撑示范区中长期评估和经验推广。论文在梳理国内外绿色发展实践与评价经验的基础上，结合北京城市副中心建设进程、下一阶段规划实施需求和绿色发展标准体系建设方向，提出以“绿色生产—绿色生活—绿色生态”为主体，以“安全韧性”和“协同共治”为支撑的“3+2”监测评估指标体系。其中，“三绿”维度与现有政策指标体系保持衔接，承担基础监测和成效评价功能；“安全韧性”和“协同共治”维度承担风险识别、跨界协同和制度创新诊断功能。该体系有助于推动副中心绿色发展评价由结果性考核向过程监测、风险预警和协同问效转变，为国家绿色发展示范区指标动态更新和城市绿色治理能力提升提供参考。
authors: 李伟峰、郝思嘉、荣月静、王国玉、袁瑞、周伟奇

title: 美丽城市群不同类型城市的绿色低碳发展模式研究
abstract: 美丽城市群是推进美丽中国建设的重要空间载体，而分类探索绿色低碳发展模式是美丽城市群建设的科学途径。以京津冀城市群为案例，论文运用熵权法与系统聚类方法识别出高质低碳引领型、均衡转型示范型、工业重载承压型与生态涵养屏障型4类城市，构建扩展STIRPAT (stochastic impacts by regression on population, affluence, and technology)模型解析各类城市碳排放的异质性驱动机制，并结合5类情景对2026—2035年碳排放趋势进行系统预测，深入探讨不同类型城市的绿色低碳发展模式。研究发现：① 区域绿色低碳发展呈现显著的结构性类型分化，“极核引领、屏障环绕、中部交错”的空间格局根植于资源禀赋差异与功能分工逻辑。② 各类城市碳排放驱动机制存在根本差异，引领型城市经济增长与碳排放的脱钩程度相对较高；承压型城市人口规模扩张对碳排放具有较强的正向锁定效应。③ 情景模拟揭示了不同发展路径的边界条件，引领型城市在经济优先情景下可于2026年前后达到碳排放峰值；示范型城市在常规情景下碳排放总体呈现平台期特征；承压型城市的情景间分化表明产业结构升级对其未来碳排放路径具有关键影响；屏障型城市对规模扩张的较高环境敏感性反映了生态阈值效应的现实约束。研究认为，可将京津冀美丽城市群的绿色低碳发展模式提炼成4类差异化模式，即“零碳创新引领”“协同稳健转型”“存量脱碳升级”“绿色价值实现”，以期为分类施策推进美丽城市群建设提供研究支撑。

title: 京津冀美丽城市建设水平的时空演化与障碍因子诊断
abstract: 美丽城市是美丽中国战略在城市尺度落实的关键载体，科学评估美丽城市建设成效对推动该战略实施具有重要意义。针对以往研究在指标体系、评价方法等方面的不足，论文从环境优美、生态宜居、绿色低碳、发展创新、安全韧性、智慧治理6个维度构建指标体系，融合多源异构数据，综合运用加权几何平均法、核密度估计、标准差椭圆及障碍度模型，测度2015—2025年京津冀美丽城市的建设水平，分析其空间格局演化及主要制约因素。结果表明：① 京津冀美丽城市建设水平显著提升，区域内部差距逐步缩小，环境优美与绿色低碳维度的持续改善是区域整体水平提升的关键因素。② 空间格局呈现稳固的核心—边缘结构，路径依赖特征明显。区域重心仅小幅移动，空间演化始终锚定京津石主轴线，整体格局已进入结构趋稳、局部微调的成熟阶段。③ 美丽城市建设均衡度随建设水平的提升呈现先降后升的非同步演进规律。京津核心区处于高水平、高均衡的协同阶段，节点城市经历单维突进导致的短期失衡后趋向高位协调，而部分外围城市建设水平提升与结构均衡改善并不同步。④ 主要障碍因子由生态环境等基础性约束向发展质量、技术创新、城市韧性与协同治理等结构性约束转变。灾害韧性与联防联控薄弱是核心城市进一步提升的主要制约，提质增效与社会韧性不足是边缘城市的长期短板，而创新产出不足是城市群共性障碍。论文构建的美丽城市建设评价体系可供其他地区参考，研究结论为京津冀美丽城市分类治理和美丽中国先行区建设提供科学依据。

title: 全周期治理视角下美丽城市指标体系研究——以京津冀某市为例
abstract: 美丽城市指标体系是量化美丽城市建设成效的重要治理工具。当前美丽城市指标体系研究存在指标构建方法有待优化，目标、指标与数据传导不明，指标监测预警反馈机制缺位等不足，难以有效支撑美丽城市建设。京津冀某市是中国生态敏感型、数字智慧型新城的典型代表，亟需构建一套契合城市资源禀赋、管理特征，适配城市全周期治理需求的美丽城市指标体系。论文聚焦将美丽城市建设目标转化为可持续监测和治理工具，从城市全周期治理视角，创新提出基于“根指标库—高频指标池”的双向交叉筛选路径，通过保留、转化、剔除、增补，形成美丽城市在地化指标集。在传统“维度层—目标层—指标层”三层指标架构基础上，提出增设“根指标层”，形成从建设理念、目标指标到监测数据传导的完整链条。同时，建立“数据采集—监测预警—反馈调整”运行管理机制，明确各指标对应的监测尺度、监测频次、适用阶段、预警条件与责任部门，推动指标体系嵌入城市治理过程。研究成果可为京津冀某市美丽城市建设、空间治理与数字化管控提供技术支撑，也能为国内同类生态敏感型、数字智慧型新城的美丽城市指标体系构建与全过程监测提供方法参考。
authors: 吴丽娟、张馨元、霍子文、陶俊搏、詹晓洁

title: 京津冀美丽城市建设成效评估与调控研究——基于SDGs本土化与融合视角
abstract: “美丽城市”是中国生态文明建设与高质量发展的重要实践载体，也是联合国可持续发展目标(sustainable development goals，SDGs)在城市尺度的本土化实现路径。论文以地级市行政辖区作为评价单元，基于SDGs本土化与融合视角，高度契合“美丽城市”建设内涵，构建涵盖环境之美、经济之美、社会之美、制度之美与文化之美5个维度的综合评价体系；整合遥感与统计数据，采用熵权法与层次分析法耦合赋权，对2015—2025年京津冀美丽城市建设成效进行测度，并从时空演化、多维协同及驱动机制等方面展开分析，识别城市类型并提出差异化调控路径。研究表明：① 京津冀美丽城市建设水平持续提升，但核心—外围梯度格局显著，区域不均衡依然突出；② 5个维度间协同与权衡并存，环境与经济社会间矛盾最突出；③ 耦合协调度整体提高但空间分异仍明显；④ 产业结构升级的短期波动对美丽城市建设成效变化有显著影响，节能环保财政支出与城镇化率未形成有效传导路径，政策效果受制于城镇化质量与治理能力；⑤ 区域城市可分为创新驱动型、政策依赖型、转型攻坚型与稳步追赶型4类，发展路径与约束差异显著。最后提出差异化调控路径与区域协同发展策略。研究可为美丽城市建设成效评估提供方法支撑，并为其他国家推进城市可持续发展提供参考。

title: 树轮蓝光强度研究进展与展望
abstract: 树轮蓝光强度(blue intensity，BI)是基于树轮图像蓝色波段灰度值的一种代用指标，具有测量效率高、成本较低、无需X射线设备等显著优势。近年来，BI指标发展迅速，已成为国际树轮气候学研究的重要前沿方向之一，并被广泛认可为树轮密度的有效经验代用指标。为进一步增进科研人员对BI技术的了解，推进BI技术的应用与发展，论文系统梳理了国内外BI研究的发展脉络，涵盖其技术演进、形成机制、区域拓展与应用进展，重点综述了自2019年以来在标准术语统一、图像获取技术、心材—边材色差校正、多指标体系构建及气候响应机制等方面的最新成果。研究表明，BI技术已形成涵盖树轮早材蓝光强度(earlywood blue intensity，EWBI)、晚材蓝光强度(latewood blue intensity，LWBI)及早晚材蓝光强度差值(delta blue intensity，DBI)在内的系统指标体系；研究区域从北半球高纬度地区逐步拓展至中低纬度及南半球；应用领域亦从夏季气温重建延伸至降水、干旱、光合有效辐射、冰川变化、森林扰动及木材定年等多个方向。尽管如此，当前BI研究仍面临若干挑战，包括心材—边材色差干扰、技术流程标准化不足、不同树种与生态区适用性差异，以及长年表区域分布不均衡等问题。未来研究应着力于加强标准术语与技术规范建设，完善高分辨率图像获取与色差校正方法，推动自动化识别、高光谱成像等新兴技术的应用；同时深化多指标融合与多圈层耦合研究，进一步提升BI在高分辨率古环境重建及地球系统科学中的应用潜力。

title: 跨区域绿色治理枢纽与空间协同机制研究——以北京城市副中心为例
abstract: 在京津冀协同发展、北京非首都功能疏解和绿色低碳转型背景下，北京城市副中心的战略功能正由北京市域内部功能承接平台，逐步拓展为统筹北京城区、副中心与北三县一体化发展的区域组织枢纽，并进一步承担以绿色低碳发展和生态环境共治为导向的绿色治理枢纽职能。论文基于绿色发展、都市圈一体化和跨界生态环境协同共治视角，将北京城区—北京城市副中心—北三县作为一个连续复合地域系统，构建“功能重组—空间耦合—生态共治—制度协同”的分析框架，系统探讨三地绿色一体化的发展进程、现状特征、空间逻辑、协同机制与优化路径。研究表明：北京城市副中心不再只是承接北京中心城区疏解功能的空间平台，而是在三地一体化系统中承担功能转换、空间组织、生态接口和制度衔接等复合功能。北京城区、副中心与北三县通过非首都功能疏解、综合交通联通、公共服务重构、绿色产业协作、潮白河—北运河—大运河文化带生态廊道共建和跨界治理制度衔接，正在形成以副中心为枢纽的北京东部绿色协同治理系统。当前，该系统仍面临行政边界分割、功能承接与承载转型不匹配、跨界通勤碳排放压力较大、产业链协作层级偏低与生态空间衔接不足等问题与约束。未来应进一步强化北京城市副中心绿色治理枢纽功能，协同推进三地功能配置、交通组织、公共服务、绿色产业、生态环境和制度机制建设，构建北京东部绿色一体化高质量发展新格局。

title: 京津冀城市群资源环境效率的时空演变与驱动因素分析
abstract: 科学识别京津冀城市群资源环境效率的时空演变特征及其驱动因素，对推进京津冀美丽城市群建设、促进资源高效利用与生态环境协同治理具有重要意义。论文基于2000—2023年京津冀城市群面板数据，结合模糊隶属度评价与XGBoost-SHAP可解释机器学习方法，揭示了资源环境综合效率及用地效率、用水效率、能源效率、生态效率和环境效率的时空演变特征，并识别了不同效率维度的主导驱动因素及其非线性影响。结果表明：① 2000—2023年，京津冀城市群资源环境效率综合指数由0.183提高至0.554，整体由低水平升至中等水平；各单要素效率均有所改善，其中用水效率长期保持较高水平。② 京津冀13个地级及以上城市的资源环境效率综合指数均有所提高，空间上长期呈现“核心高、外围低”的格局。高水平区域尚未扩展至全域，但中高值区域范围逐步扩大。③ 驱动因素分析表明，绿色创新和数字化水平是资源环境综合效率的主要驱动因素，不同单要素效率的主导因素存在差异，各因素作用普遍具有阈值效应和非线性特征。④ 驱动因素交互作用结果显示，绿色创新在多数高强度交互组合中发挥关键连接作用，尤其与产业结构升级、交通基础设施协同作用较强；用水效率和能源效率对多因素共同作用更为敏感。上述研究结论可为京津冀美丽城市群建设和差异化资源环境治理提供参考。

title: 食品环境对肥胖影响的研究进展及分析框架——基于时空行为的视角
abstract: 食品环境对肥胖的影响是健康地理学和行为地理学研究的前沿议题，而时空行为视角为深化该议题提供了重要分析思路。论文首先从指标测度、影响分析、机制研究三个方面回顾并评述当前食品环境与肥胖关系的理论及实证文献，指出既往研究未能精准测度居民真实食品环境暴露、鲜少关注食品环境影响肥胖的时空效应、未能阐明食品环境影响肥胖的行为机制和时空过程。为深化食品环境与肥胖关系的研究，论文基于时空行为视角提出了食品环境影响肥胖的分析框架。首先，精准刻画中国情境下居民真实食品环境暴露的时空间特征；然后，通过纵向研究设计识别食品环境与肥胖的因果关联及其时空效应；最后，分析膳食行为的中介作用并厘清“食品环境→膳食行为→肥胖状态”路径的时空形成过程。这一框架有望推进关于地理环境暴露与健康关系的理论发展，为城市食品环境优化提供以人为本的精细化干预思路。

title: 西方政治地理学中的冲突研究进展
abstract: 冲突是西方政治地理学解析空间权力关系的核心议题。论文基于主流英文地理学文献的系统梳理，围绕“冲突如何在空间中生成、隐伏并发生后期演化分异”这一核心问题，厘清了冲突的政治地理内涵，整合重构了直接冲突(物质空间)、结构性冲突(制度空间)与文化冲突(符号空间)的分析框架。研究指出，显性暴力中止后的冲突后期(即“后冲突”状态)并非冲突的终结，而是冲突发生空间解耦的错位状态：表层物质空间的直接冲突虽被强制中止，深层制度空间的结构性冲突与符号空间的文化冲突仍在持续发酵。进一步揭示了冲突后期是否陷入新一轮冲突的空间动态转化逻辑：外部干预主导的空间机械分割易固化深层对立，诱发制度与文化冲突向上尺度溢出并重燃直接冲突；内部力量主导的空间有机整合则更能推动三元空间协同去边界化，促使排斥性边界转化为共享网络，并最终消解冲突、走向“正和平”。

title: 新质生产力赋能中国城市旅游韧性的空间效应
abstract: 提升旅游系统韧性是应对复杂外部冲击、实现旅游产业高质量发展的关键命题。新质生产力作为先进生产力质态，为重塑旅游产业抗逆机制提供了核心内生动力。论文基于2011—2023年中国278个地级及以上城市面板数据，结合随机森林算法构建多维评价体系，并综合运用空间面板杜宾模型，系统考察了新质生产力驱动城市旅游韧性提升的空间溢出效应。研究发现：① 空间演化上，新质生产力与旅游韧性存在显著的轨迹协同，共同呈现由“极化集聚”向“网络均衡”的多极演进特征。② 新质生产力不仅显著强化本地旅游韧性，更产生强烈的空间网络溢出，且具备多维非对称传导特征。其中，数字经济对适应与调整力发挥统领性驱动作用，绿色转型在更新与重构维度的溢出效应最为突出，自主创新则主导本地抵抗与恢复力的夯实。③ 该驱动效应呈现显著的核心—外围空间异质性与阶段激活的时间动态特征。大型城市扮演着区域韧性辐射源的关键角色，而在面临极端外部扰动时，新质生产力的总体驱动效应跃升，凸显了其系统稳定器功能。研究将新质生产力引入旅游韧性分析框架，揭示了其超地理溢出与网络共生的独特属性，为实施数字化靶向干预、构建跨域韧性共同体以及边缘城市差异化破局提供了精准的决策支撑。

title: 工业用地容积率规制对工业绿色发展的影响及其传导机制
abstract: 探究工业用地容积率规制对工业绿色发展的作用机理，可为优化土地要素配置和助推工业绿色转型提供科学参考。论文基于2009—2022年中国281个地级及以上城市面板数据，采用超效率SBM-DEA模型测算兼顾减污降碳的工业绿色发展水平，构建固定效应、机制检验和门槛效应模型检验工业用地容积率规制对工业绿色发展的影响与传导机制。结果表明：① 研究期内，各城市容积率规制强度和工业绿色发展水平均显著提升，长三角、珠三角城市群将规制强度提升至1.445以上并渐进形成带状集聚，工业绿色发展高值区持续向区域产业优势城市聚拢，峰值由初期的0.301跃升至1.116。② 容积率规制有效推动了工业绿色发展，且该赋能效应因区位禀赋和行业属性不同而存有差异。③ 容积率规制可通过优化土地配置结构和激发绿色技术创新，间接驱动地区工业绿色发展，同时，该政策的绿色转型效应伴随城市内企业数字化转型发展还呈现递增规律。地方政府应立足城市演进阶段与行业特征，推行“因地制宜、分类施策”的工业用地容积率规制策略，健全土地配置优化与绿色技术创新协同机制，夯实数字赋能底座，充分释放容积率规制的绿色转型潜能。

title: 传统商业街区居民地方认同与空间正义感知研究——基于表征与非表征视角
abstract: 传统商业街区作为具有深厚历史文化内涵的商业区域，发展至今已成为当地的记忆符号与特殊象征。如何平衡商业开发与在地留存，顺应人本规划的发展趋势以进一步实现空间正义与强化居民地方认同，是其更新重点。结合现有城市发展目标及城市更新理念，在假设街区表征、非表征与居民地方认同相互作用的理论框架基础上引入街区居民空间正义感知，构建传统商业街区环境、居民行动与态度作用关系的概念模型，将北京市隆福寺商业街区这一典型城市更新实践作为研究案例，运用结构方程模型加以验证，并通过问卷调研、扎根理论及IPA (importance-performance analysis)-Kano模型对研究区域的后续更新优化方向及策略进行补充，相较于以往研究方法更为科学、全面。研究结果表明：① 街区表征、非表征及街区居民空间正义感知均显著影响街区居民地方认同，通过空间符号、空间体验、空间感知作用于街区居民的空间情感；② 居民空间正义感知在“表征、非表征—地方认同”作用路径中起到部分中介作用，且其对地方认同的影响作用最强；③ 通过IPA-Kano模型构建街区表征、非表征要素显隐性重要性矩阵，确定了历史留存、文化活动、风俗习惯及街区议事为隆福寺商业街区后续核心优化要素。研究验证了概念模型的科学性与适配性，可为传统商业街区更新提供可参考路径。

title: 广州市大型商圈吸引力空间格局识别及其影响因素对比
abstract: 随着城市化进程的加速，城市商业格局从单中心逐渐向双中心、多中心演变，而现有研究对多中心趋势下不同类型商圈吸引力空间格局及其影响因素差异的探讨尚有不足。论文以广州市不同城市化时期规划并建成的三个大型商圈——传统步行街商圈北京路—海珠广场、成熟高端商圈天河路—珠江新城和新晋热门商圈长隆—万博为研究对象，基于多源数据刻画各商圈的商业结构及吸引力特征，并构建负二项回归模型，探讨社区社会属性、社区商业建成环境、社区交通可达性等因素对商圈客流量的影响程度差异，发现：① 三个商圈在客流量、可达性和商业构成上有明显差异，成熟高端商圈的客流量最多、可达性最好、设施量最多且多样性最高；新晋热门商圈的客流量最少、可达性最差、设施量最少且多样性最低；② 不同商圈的服务范围呈现显著的空间分异特征，成熟高端商圈的服务范围最大，新晋热门商圈的服务范围最小且其距离衰减也最为明显；③ 社区至商圈的流动距离是制约社区至商圈客流量的首要因素，社区年龄结构及拥有汽车比例对不同商圈的客流影响有所差异。其中，社区拥有汽车比例制约前往传统步行街商圈的客流量，但促进前往成熟高端商圈和新晋热门商圈的客流量。成熟高端商圈吸引青年和中年群体，但新晋热门商圈主要吸引青年群体，所有商圈都不吸引老年群体。研究对比了广州市不同定位商圈的特征及客流量影响因素，有利于更好地认识城市商业布局及发展历程，并为未来广州市商业功能区规划提供切实的建议与优化策略。

title: 雅鲁藏布江流域冰前湖1990—2025年悬浮物浓度变化及影响因素研究
abstract: 冰前湖悬浮物浓度变化能够直接反映冰川融水携带的悬浮沉积物含量，是气候变化引起冰川消融与侵蚀的敏感指标。论文以雅鲁藏布江流域冰前湖为研究对象，结合野外实测浊度数据(n=110)与实验室测定的悬浮物浓度(suspended sediment concentration，SSC)数据(n=47)，构建了基于Landsat系列影像的“浊度遥感反演—SSC转换估算”两步法框架，波段敏感性分析表明红光波段(B4)对高浑浊水体响应最强(r=0.73)。多种函数模型对比结果显示，S曲线模型在反演精度与稳定性方面表现最优(R2=0.57，RMSE=8.16 FNU)，SSC和浊度之间的非线性关系预测结果与实测结果基本一致(R2=0.80，RMSE=10.0 mg/L)，据此实现了1990—2025年冰前湖SSC的长时序重建。结果表明，流域尺度冰前湖SSC整体呈现显著下降趋势，其中春季降幅最为明显。空间上，冰前湖SSC表现出显著异质性，整体呈“上游高、下游低”的分布格局。结合气象资料的初步分析表明，流域增温引起的水热条件变化是冰前湖SSC变化的关键驱动力。气温升高通过调节积雪融化节律，强化冰川融水稀释效应，进而影响物源供给与湖泊水动力过程，共同控制了冰前湖SSC的长期演变。高原冰前湖SSC的演变机制较为复杂，研究为认识雅江流域悬浮物的循环过程及其未来变化提供了重要依据，也为高原冰前湖悬浮物动态监测与冰冻圈变化影响评估提供了方法支撑与区域证据。
authors: 武襄君、朱立平、黄磊、杨弘毅、刘翀、鞠建廷

title: 从“主体”到“共主体”：义工与地方旅游企业价值共创路径分析
abstract: 随着大众旅游需求迭代与消费形态多元化，以“以工换宿”为代表的弹性用工模式正在重塑旅游目的地的劳动力组织方式与个体旅行者的地方实践。论文以丽江背包十年青年旅社这一地方旅游企业的典型代表为案例，运用自我民族志、半结构化访谈等质性方法，将价值共创理论与主体间性理论进行创新性结合来建立框架，考察个体旅行者在异地的劳动嵌入如何成为其与地方企业协同创造价值的机制。研究发现，在地方旅游企业的弹性用工实践中，以劳动换宿为形式的义工与青年旅社的价值共创包含4个相互关联的维度：经济协同是物质基础，义工通过劳动置换节省食宿成本，青年旅社获得弹性劳动力；社交融合是关系纽带，义工社交圈层拓展，青年旅社文化活力再生；形象共建是符号媒介，义工在他人目光中确认自我价值，青年旅社品牌借助个体叙事获得传播；价值拓展是最终归宿，多方主体突破角色边界，形成价值共同体。在此基础上，双方关系经历从“价值共识”到“价值共赢”再到“价值共生”的三阶段演进，并形成“共识—共赢—共生—新共识”的动态循环。研究的理论贡献在于丰富了价值共创理论与主体间性理论在旅游领域的应用，拓展了人地关系在非标准化就业情境下的解释边界，也为理解新时代旅游劳动力流动、地方文化再生产与小微企业经营转型提供了新的分析框架。

title: 中小学社会情感学习如何融入课程体系——基于芬兰国家核心课程的考察
abstract: 芬兰以课程综合改革带动社会情感学习的系统性变革。社会情感学习在国家课程体系中实现全科目的横向覆盖和中小幼全学段的纵向贯通。三级支持体系为社会情感学习全过程提供保障。地方课程体系通过课程本土化、项目常态化和支持小组化，提升社会情感学习与地方的适配性。戏剧教学方式的推广、教师教育体系的完善和校家社协同网络的构建，共同确保社会情感学习落地。综合我国社会情感学习实践，应进一步提升教师社会情感教学的准备程度...
